title: The "Confirm it's you" box's 5-wrong-tries lockout does not hold against a burst of parallel guesses
what_happens: POST /api/auth/confirm's password/code check (src/lib/security/factors.ts verifyFactor) reads the failure count with failuresOver(key, 5) before the slow bcrypt.compare runs, and only records a failure with addFailure(key, ...) after that compare resolves. Sent one request at a time, the 6th wrong guess in 15 minutes is refused with 429 before any password check runs. Sent together, every request in the burst reads the same pre-burst failure count (0) before any of them finishes bcrypt and writes its own failure back, so the whole burst is let through to a real password check (401, not 429): the 5-attempt lockout never engages. Verified live against the pass-4 server on port 3214: signed in as a staff account with no prior failures, fired 20 POST /api/auth/confirm requests in parallel with wrong passwords (same scope/action), and got 20x 401 (every one actually checked against bcrypt), not the 5x 401 + 15x 429 the design calls for. Reproduced twice (officerA, then a fresh collector session before its own counter had failures; once an account's counter is already past 5 from an earlier burst, later bursts on that same account correctly get 429, which only confirms the counter itself is fine -- it is the order of the read and the write around the awaited bcrypt call that races).
what_should_happen: A burst of parallel guesses against the same account's step-up confirmation should be limited the same way sequential guesses are: at most 5 of any window of wrong attempts should ever reach bcrypt.compare; the rest should get 429 before the password is touched. This needs either a lock/counter that is reserved before the await (not just updated after it), or an atomic increment-then-check in the rate limiter for this key.
repro: node tests/qa/pass4/server.mjs start --port 3214 --frozen --ticking --instance redsec2; then npx vitest run --config vitest.qa4.config.ts tests/qa/pass4/hunt-redsec2.test.ts (the one test logs in as officerB -- an account whose confirm-fail counter has no prior failures this server run -- and fires 20 parallel POST /api/auth/confirm with wrong passwords; it currently gets about 20 x 401 instead of at most 5 x 401 + the rest 429). Re-running the test against an account that already failed 5+ times this server session will not reproduce it (the counter is already past the gate by then); use a fresh account or restart the server to see it again.
evidence: tests/qa/pass4/hunt-redsec2.test.ts (hunt-redsec2-1, it.fails, passes as a confirmed-still-open bug when run against an account with a clean failure counter); live transcripts: officerA burst of 60 parallel wrong guesses -> 60x 401, then the very next single guess -> 429 "Too many wrong tries"; collector burst of 20 parallel wrong guesses (fresh at the time) -> 20x 401; server log data/aws-cache/qa/run/srv-3214.log shows no crash, i.e. this is the server's actual behaviour under concurrency, not an error path
root_cause_guess: src/lib/security/factors.ts:26-33 verifyFactor (failuresOver(key,5) checked before, addFailure(key,...) called only after, the awaited bcrypt.compare in checkOne); src/lib/rate-limit.ts failuresOver/addFailure (correct for sequential calls, not safe against concurrent reads of the same key before any of them has written back)
class: race condition (TOCTOU) in a security rate limiter, defeating a brute-force lockout under concurrency
not_a_bug_note: The same checkRateLimit() used for login (src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts) increments its bucket synchronously at the very start of the request, before any password check, so sequential and parallel login attempts are both counted correctly; this race is specific to the confirm/step-up path's failuresOver+addFailure pattern, where the write is deferred past an awaited bcrypt call.
